column1: Throughout this book we have summarized the tax system with a single variable, T. In our models, the policy instrument is the level of taxation that the government chooses; we have ignored the issue of how the government raises this tax revenue. In practice, however, taxes are not lump-sum payments but are levied on some type of economic activity. The U.S. federal government raises some revenue by taxing personal income (46 percent of tax revenue in 2014), some by taxing payrolls (34 percent), some by taxing corporate profits (11 percent), and some from other sources (6 percent).
